sae_sycophancy_audit.sae_formulation:
To cleanly isolate the "Sycophancy Feature" from standard instruction-following features within the residual stream, we train a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) utilizing an L0 constraint over a high-dimensional dictionary. Let the residual stream activations at layer $l$ be denoted as $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
The SAE consists of an encoder $f_e$ and a decoder $f_d$: $z = f_e(x) = \text{ReLU}(W_e x + b_e)$ $\hat{x} = f_d(z) = W_d z + b_d$
Given the dictionary size $D = 2.1 \times 10^6$ and a target sparsity $L_0 = 64$, the training objective function is formulated to minimize reconstruction error while enforcing strict sparsity via an approximation of the $L_0$ norm. We employ an $L_1$ penalty weighted by $\lambda$ to induce the desired $L_0$ sparsity.
$\mathcal{L}_{\text{SAE}} = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim \mathcal{D}} \left[ ||x - \hat{x}||_2^2 + \lambda ||z||_1 \right]$
To specifically isolate the Sycophancy Feature ($v_{\text{syc}}$), we introduce a contrastive term into the objective. Let $\mathcal{D}_{\text{biased}}$ be a dataset of prompts with biased premises and $\mathcal{D}_{\text{neutral}}$ be a dataset of neutral prompts. We compute the mean activations $\bar{x}_{\text{biased}}$ and $\bar{x}_{\text{neutral}}$.
The Sycophancy Feature is defined as the dictionary element $d_k$ (where $d_k$ is the $k$-th column of $W_d$) that maximizes the projection difference: $\arg\max_{k} \left( d_k^T (\bar{x}_{\text{biased}} - \bar{x}_{\text{neutral}}) \right)$
We adjust the objective to penalize activation of this feature $k$ when training on neutral instructions to untangle it from instruction following: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{SAE}} + \gamma \mathbb{E}_{x \sim \mathcal{D}_{\text{neutral}}} [z_k^2]$
sae_sycophancy_audit.causal_mediation_flow:
The causal mediation analysis protocol maps the shift in self-attention weights of Layer 8, Head 11 (L8H11) when subjected to biased versus neutral premises.
Protocol Steps: 1. Baseline Activation: Run a forward pass over a set of neutral prompts ($P_{\text{neutral}}$) and record the self-attention probability matrix $A^{(8,11)}_{\text{neutral}}$. 2. Counterfactual Activation: Run a forward pass over paired biased prompts ($P_{\text{biased}}$) and record the self-attention probability matrix $A^{(8,11)}_{\text{biased}}$. 3. Activation Patching (Mediation): - Initiate a forward pass on a neutral prompt $P_{\text{neutral}}$. - At Layer 8, intercept the computation of Head 11. - Replace the output of L8H11 with the cached output generated by $P_{\text{biased}}$. - Let the forward pass complete to yield the patched logits $\hat{y}_{\text{patched}}$. 4. Compute Direct and Indirect Effects: - Total Effect (TE) = Logit($y_{\text{syc}} | P_{\text{biased}}$) - Logit($y_{\text{syc}} | P_{\text{neutral}}$) - Natural Indirect Effect (NIE) of L8H11 = Logit($y_{\text{syc}} | P_{\text{neutral}}, \text{do}(\text{L8H11} = \text{L8H11}(P_{\text{biased}}))$) - Logit($y_{\text{syc}} | P_{\text{neutral}}$) 5. Evaluate Shift: The attention shift $\Delta A = A^{(8,11)}_{\text{biased}} - A^{(8,11)}_{\text{neutral}}$ is analyzed. If NIE/TE is significantly high, L8H11 acts as a primary causal mediator for the Sycophancy Attractor, and $\Delta A$ reveals the tokens (e.g., the biased premise tokens) that L8H11 disproportionately attends to.
sae_sycophancy_audit.steering_equations:
To mitigate the Sycophancy Attractor, we design a closed-loop gradient steering algorithm that intercepts inference activations at Layer 24 (L24) and orthogonally projects the hidden states.
Let $h_{24}$ be the residual stream activation at Layer 24. Let $v_{\text{syc}} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be the normalized Sycophancy Feature vector identified via the SAE ($||v_{\text{syc}}||_2 = 1$).
The projection matrix $P_{\perp}$ orthogonal to the Sycophancy Feature is defined as: $P_{\perp} = I - v_{\text{syc}} v_{\text{syc}}^T$
The steered activation $h'_{24}$ is computed by removing the component parallel to $v_{\text{syc}}$: $h'_{24} = P_{\perp} h_{24} = h_{24} - (v_{\text{syc}}^T h_{24}) v_{\text{syc}}$
To evaluate the real-time efficacy of this steering, we calculate the Sycophancy Index (SI) shift. Let the probability of generating a sycophantic continuation before and after steering be $p(y_{\text{syc}} | h_{24})$ and $p(y_{\text{syc}} | h'_{24})$, respectively.
The SI is defined as the log-odds of the sycophantic token: $\text{SI} = \log \frac{p(y_{\text{syc}})}{1 - p(y_{\text{syc}})}$
The resultant SI shift ($\Delta \text{SI}$) is: $\Delta \text{SI} = \text{SI}(h'_{24}) - \text{SI}(h_{24})$
A successful closed-loop intervention yields a substantially negative $\Delta \text{SI}$, indicating that the model's latent trajectory has been successfully repulsed from the Sycophancy Attractor basin.
